evals.name: diff-scope-fix
evals.prompt: The sonar server is crawling again today. I just added a few classes to this shop project on my current branch — can you run a local static analysis on just my changes (no sonar server) and fix whatever it flags? The project is a plain Maven project at the current working directory.
evals.expected_output: Runs the local-scan orchestrator scoped to the git diff (UserRepository.java, PaymentService.java, OrderUtil.java), surfaces the planted findings (SQL injection, weak MD5 hash, hardcoded secret, == string comparison, empty catch, unused variable, complex method), and fixes them in the source files. Does not touch the committed clean baseline. Does not invent findings beyond what the tools report.
assertions: Ran the real analyzers (orchestrator or pmd/spotbugs/semgrep CLIs); findings.json present
Scope respected: only the three new classes changed, not the committed baseline
SQL injection fixed with a parameterized PreparedStatement
Weak MD5 hashing replaced with a strong algorithm
No fabricated findings beyond actual tool output

evals.name: all-scope
evals.prompt: /r:code-scan ALL — go over the whole shop project with the local analyzers (pmd, spotbugs, semgrep) instead of the SonarQube server and fix the issues you find.
evals.expected_output: Runs the orchestrator with --scope all over the whole project, reports findings across all classes, and fixes them. Mentions which tools ran (and any that were skipped because not installed).
assertions: Used whole-project scope (--scope all), not just the diff
Ran all three analyzers and named which ran; findings across multiple classes
Fixed SQL injection, weak MD5, and == comparison at minimum

evals.name: scoped-class-security
evals.prompt: Can you locally scan PaymentService for security and bug issues without using the sonar server, and fix what you find? Keep it scoped to that class.
evals.expected_output: Runs the orchestrator filtered to PaymentService (--filter PaymentService), reports its findings (weak MD5 hashing, hardcoded API secret, == string comparison), fixes them, and does not modify the other classes.
assertions: Fix touches ONLY PaymentService.java, not the other classes
Fixed weak MD5 and == comparison (ideally flags hardcoded secret)
Ran the real analyzers; findings.json present

evals.name: routing-triggers
evals.prompt: run pmd and spotbugs over what I changed and fix what they find
evals.expected_output: code-scan loads, runs PMD + SpotBugs/find-sec-bugs + Semgrep as local CLIs over the diff, then triages and fixes the findings. No server, no tokens.

evals.name: routing-excludes-code-bugs
evals.prompt: read through my changes and spot the logic mistakes
evals.expected_output: A judgement-based hunt is code-bugs' job; code-scan must not load, because it runs mechanical analyzers rather than reading for intent.
